note: The contract between scripts/releve_cost.py and js/cost.js. Token counts are deliberately round so every expected dollar figure can be checked by hand against data/rates.json. expect.tokens is a partial dict: only the keys listed are asserted. expect.uncached is asserted only where present.

cases.name: opus5-input-only
cases.why: Base input rate. 1M tokens at $5/MTok.

cases.name: opus5-output-only
cases.why: Base output rate. 1M tokens at $25/MTok.

cases.name: opus5-cache-read
cases.why: Cache read is 0.1x input, so $0.50/MTok. 10M reads is $5.00. This is the single largest line on a real statement.

cases.name: opus5-cache-write-5m
cases.why: 5-minute cache write is 1.25x input, so $6.25/MTok.

cases.name: opus5-cache-write-1h
cases.why: Rule 3. 1-hour cache write is 2.0x input, so $10.00/MTok, not the 1.25x the old script charged everything.

cases.name: opus5-cache-write-both-ttls
cases.why: Both TTLs on one turn, each at its own multiplier: 20k at 6.25 plus 8k at 10.00.

cases.name: opus5-realistic-turn
cases.why: The shape of an actual mid-session turn: small fresh input, large cache read, some cache written.

cases.name: opus5-fast-mode
cases.why: Rule 4. speed: fast bills $10/$50, double standard. A fast session priced at standard rates is under-reported by half.

cases.name: opus5-fast-mode-cache
cases.why: Fast mode doubles the base input rate, and cache rates derive from base input, so a 5m write costs 12.50/MTok. Stated as an assumption in rates.json, not verified.

cases.name: opus5-speed-standard-explicit
cases.why: An explicit speed: standard must not trip the override lookup.

cases.name: opus5-thinking-is-a-label
cases.why: thinking_tokens are already inside output_tokens. Carried as a label, never added to cost. 10k output at $25/MTok is $0.25 whether 8k of it was reasoning or none.

cases.name: iterations-single-agrees-with-top-level
cases.why: Rule 5, the common case. 77,063 of 77,072 real turns with an iterations array have exactly one entry, and it equals the top-level counters. Reading the array is a no-op here, which is what makes it safe to always prefer it.

cases.name: iterations-multi-replaces-top-level
cases.why: Rule 5, the case that matters. On a multi-iteration turn the top-level counters hold only the LAST iteration, verified on 9 of 9 real ones, so the sum is the billable figure. Reading the top level alone would charge 400k input where 1M was billed.

cases.name: iterations-never-added-to-top-level
cases.why: The other half of Rule 5. Summing the array AND the top level would bill 1.4M input here instead of 1M. The array replaces, it does not augment.

cases.name: iterations-carry-the-ttl-split
cases.why: Every real iteration carries its own cache_creation split, so the 5m and 1h totals accumulate across iterations at their own multipliers.

cases.name: iterations-with-zero-top-level
cases.why: Three real turns record zeros at the top level and the whole turn inside iterations, hiding 2M cache-read tokens. Preferring the array recovers them.

cases.name: empty-iterations-array-falls-back
cases.why: An empty array is not a breakdown. 38,356 real turns have no iterations at all, and they must still price off the top-level counters.

cases.name: opus5-dated-model-id
cases.why: Longest declared prefix. A dated snapshot id resolves to its family rate rather than falling through to UNPRICED.

cases.name: opus5-region-prefixed-id
cases.why: Bedrock and Vertex ids carry a region prefix. Suffix match keeps them priced at API rates, which the Method page states is an approximation for those backends.

cases.name: fable5-mixed
cases.why: Fable 5 at $10/$50 is double Opus 5. The old script priced it at Sonnet 4, under-reporting by roughly 70%.

cases.name: sonnet5-before-price-change
cases.why: Dated periods. On 2026-08-31 Sonnet 5 is still on introductory pricing, $2/$10.

cases.name: sonnet5-on-price-change
cases.why: On 2026-09-01 the same turn costs $3/$15. A single flat rate would misprice one side of this boundary.

cases.name: sonnet5-cache-read-follows-the-period
cases.why: Cache rates derive from that period's input rate, so the cache read also changes on 2026-09-01: 0.2 becomes 0.3.

cases.name: sonnet5-cache-read-before-change
cases.why: The same turn a month earlier reads at 0.2, not 0.3.

cases.name: sonnet5-undated-turn-uses-current-rates
cases.why: With no date, the last period wins. An undated turn is priced at today's rate rather than silently at the cheapest one.

cases.name: sonnet46-input-and-cache-write
cases.why: Sonnet 4.6 at $3/$15, 5m write at 3.75.

cases.name: haiku45-all-three
cases.why: Haiku 4.5 at $1/$5, read at 0.10.

cases.name: haiku35-dated-id
cases.why: The older naming shape, claude-3-5-haiku-*, at $0.80/MTok input.

cases.name: tier-standard-explicit
cases.why: The tier every real turn carries. Multiplier 1.0, nothing assumed.

cases.name: tier-batch-halves-every-rate
cases.why: Batch is half price, and the cache rates derive from the halved input: read becomes 0.25/MTok, not 0.50.

cases.name: tier-batch-cache-write
cases.why: A 5m write on batch is 1.25x the halved input, so 3.125/MTok.

cases.name: tier-priority-priced-at-standard-and-flagged
cases.why: Priority carries a premium that is not a flat multiple of standard. Priced at standard and flagged, so the page can say the figure is a floor rather than quietly inventing a premium.

cases.name: tier-unknown-is-flagged-not-discounted
cases.why: A tier the rate card has never heard of must not silently change the bill, and must not pass unremarked either.

cases.name: unpriced-known-non-anthropic
cases.why: Rule 2. kimi-k3 is declared with no rate. Its tokens are counted and reported in their own bucket, and its cost is not a number at all rather than zero.

cases.name: unpriced-unknown-model
cases.why: Rule 2, the case that broke the old script. A model absent from the rate card lands in UNPRICED. It is never quietly priced as some other model.

cases.name: unpriced-missing-model
cases.why: A turn with usage but no model field cannot be priced and must not be attributed to anything.

cases.name: excluded-synthetic
cases.why: Claude Code writes <synthetic> for locally generated messages. Never billed, so excluded outright and counted separately rather than priced at zero.

cases.name: legacy-flat-cache-creation
cases.why: Older transcripts carry only cache_creation_input_tokens with no TTL split. Treated as 5m, the default TTL, and the row is flagged estimated so the site can say which totals are approximate.

cases.name: legacy-empty-split-object
cases.why: An empty cache_creation object carries no split either, so it falls back the same way and is still flagged.

cases.name: split-with-only-the-1h-key
cases.why: A split object naming just one TTL is still a split. Nothing is estimated.

cases.name: split-present-and-zero-is-not-estimated
cases.why: A turn that wrote no cache but declares the split keys is exact, not estimated. Guards against flagging most of a real transcript.

cases.name: zero-cache-creation-is-not-estimated
cases.why: A flat zero is not an estimate of anything.

cases.name: all-zero-usage
cases.why: A turn that billed nothing is priced and worth zero. Distinct from unpriced.

cases.name: no-usage-object
cases.why: Some assistant entries carry no usage at all. They must contribute zero rather than raise.

cases.name: counterfactual-no-cache
cases.why: The cache-lab number. Actual is $1.13; the same turn with no cache, every read and write repriced as fresh input, is $5.505. That 4.9x gap is the story the dashboard tells.

cases.name: counterfactual-includes-output-unchanged
cases.why: The counterfactual reprices input only. Output is output either way.

dedup.name: one-response-many-blocks
dedup.why: Rule 6. A response that thought, spoke and called a tool is written as three entries with three uuids, each repeating the same usage. All three must key to one billed response, or the tokens are counted three times.

dedup.name: distinct-responses-stay-distinct
dedup.why: The rule must not over-collapse: two real responses are two bills.

dedup.name: no-message-id-falls-back-to-uuid
dedup.why: An entry with no message.id is still one turn. Falling back to the uuid counts it once rather than dropping it or merging every such entry together.
